title: Five policies to lower heating bills and accelerate heat pump adoption in Illinois
summary: RMI models Illinois heat pump bills and upfront costs and recommends incentives, 0% financing, rate design, AC-to-heat-pump and new-construction policies.

assertions.quote: Households heated with propane and electric resistance see the largest annual bill savings ($930 and $1,110, respectively) with all-electric heat pumps.
residents upgrading from electric resistance or propane furnaces could reduce their annual energy bills by an average of $1,110 and $930
For gas-heated homes, the bill savings vary by heat pump design and utility territory.
they typically have an up-front cost premium relative to traditional system replacements
Full-load cold climate heat pumps replace both a furnace or boiler and an air conditioner (AC).
a hybrid ASHP sized to the cooling load and paired with the existing furnace for supplemental heat (i.e., part-load ASHP) reduces energy bills the most
replacing a failing central AC represents one of the easiest and lowest-cost opportunities to scale ASHP adoption
they still have a cost premium relative to AC-only replacements — typically around $1,000 to $2,000
to ComEd’s electric heating rate, which offers lower electricity prices
Weatherization can play a critical role in improving heat pump affordability
would likely make a heat pump less expensive than installing a new AC and furnace
heat pumps installed today can cut lifetime operational emissions by over 50% compared to a gas furnace in Illinois
Heat pump water heaters (HPWHs) can also deliver meaningful bill savings, as they are three to four times more efficient than conventional units.

verdicts.note: Heat pump water heaters have energy factors of about 3-4 versus about 0.9 for resistance and 0.6-0.7 for gas tanks.
